site.name: Q-Day India
site.tagline: Scan India's websites and your code for quantum risk — then fix it.
site.description: A weekly Quantum Readiness Index of Indian websites and a private, in-browser scanner for quantum-vulnerable cryptography in your code.

home.scanCodeNote: Runs entirely in your browser. Your code is never uploaded.
home.statPq: of tracked Indian sites use quantum-safe key exchange
home.sectorChartDesc: Share of reachable tracked sites in each sector by quantum key-exchange grade.

grade.A+: Quantum-safe key exchange by default; legacy TLS disabled
grade.A: Quantum-safe key exchange by default; legacy TLS still enabled
grade.B: Supports a post-quantum hybrid, but not negotiated by default
grade.C: TLS 1.3 without post-quantum key exchange — not yet quantum-safe
grade.F: Only TLS below 1.2, or an invalid certificate chain
grade.none: Not graded — the host could not be reached

flags.SHA1_IN_CHAIN: SHA-1 signature in the certificate chain

index.title: Quantum Readiness Index
index.intro: Weekly TLS checks of public Indian websites. The grade reflects key exchange only — post-quantum certificates do not exist in the public web PKI yet.
index.unverifiedHelp: This hostname was drafted from public information and has not yet been confirmed by a maintainer.

hndl.label: Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later exposure
hndl.help: How much recorded traffic could be decrypted later by a quantum computer, weighted by how long this sector's data stays sensitive. 0 = uses quantum-safe key exchange.

cert.quantumStatus: Classical (industry-wide — PQ certificates not yet available in WebPKI)
